filter1.cutoff.notes: 0=fully closed, 1=fully open. Calibrated 2026-07-31 via the audio-rendering pipeline (see docs/PARAMETER_SCHEMA.md item 2 and reference-serum-verify-audio-pipeline): an 11-point sweep on lowpass_24 fed white noise, measuring 85%-energy spectral rolloff, gives 0.05->21.5Hz through 1.00->14427.2Hz, roughly log-linear through the middle with some flattening at both extremes. Treat as the best current reference table, not a closed-form formula (rolloff85 is a proxy for -3dB point, and the flattening at the extremes could be a real curve feature or a proxy artifact, not disambiguated). Still `uncertain` because this table is specific to lowpass_24 -- not independently confirmed for every other filter type in the enum above (comb/formant/moog/etc. plausibly use a different Freq curve or a different role for this knob entirely). Confirmed 2026-08-01 via VST3 binary string mining: DistComb1BP/1LP/2BP/2LP's 'COMBFRQ' UI knob (previously flagged as an unconfirmed possible 5th filter param) is THIS param under a type-specific label, not a separate one -- the binary's automatable-param enum for VoiceFilter has no separate Comb-frequency ID, and 'CombFrq'/'LP Frq'/'HP Frq' sit adjacent in the string table as per-type label variants of kParamFreq (the same pattern as kParamVar's per-type relabeling below).

filter2.cutoff.notes: 0=fully closed, 1=fully open. Calibrated 2026-07-31 via the audio-rendering pipeline (see docs/PARAMETER_SCHEMA.md item 2 and reference-serum-verify-audio-pipeline): an 11-point sweep on lowpass_24 fed white noise, measuring 85%-energy spectral rolloff, gives 0.05->21.5Hz through 1.00->14427.2Hz, roughly log-linear through the middle with some flattening at both extremes. Treat as the best current reference table, not a closed-form formula (rolloff85 is a proxy for -3dB point, and the flattening at the extremes could be a real curve feature or a proxy artifact, not disambiguated). Still `uncertain` because this table is specific to lowpass_24 -- not independently confirmed for every other filter type in the enum above (comb/formant/moog/etc. plausibly use a different Freq curve or a different role for this knob entirely). Confirmed 2026-08-01 via VST3 binary string mining: DistComb1BP/1LP/2BP/2LP's 'COMBFRQ' UI knob (previously flagged as an unconfirmed possible 5th filter param) is THIS param under a type-specific label, not a separate one -- the binary's automatable-param enum for VoiceFilter has no separate Comb-frequency ID, and 'CombFrq'/'LP Frq'/'HP Frq' sit adjacent in the string table as per-type label variants of kParamFreq (the same pattern as kParamVar's per-type relabeling below).

global.fx_bus1_destination.notes: Decoded 2026-07-30 by a full-corpus survey (626 real Factory presets, 14 with this key present): every value observed was 1.0 or 2.0, NEVER 0.0 or 3.0 -- exactly the two RoutingSlot.kParamRoutingDest ordinals that make sense as a post-FX bus return (kRoutingDestMaster=1: straight to main output; kRoutingDestDirect=2: a separate bypass path) and never the two that wouldn't (kRoutingDestFilter=0: nonsensical, already downstream of the filter stage; kRoutingDestNone=3: would silence the whole processed bus). Shares the same MEANING as RoutingSlot's kParamRoutingDest but NOT the same storage kind -- unlike RoutingSlot (which stores this enum as a literal string, e.g. 'kRoutingDestFilter'), Global0 stores it as a raw float ordinal (1.0/2.0), confirmed directly against real Factory CBOR. kind stays 'float' here for that reason; GlobalSpec.fx_bus1_destination/mapping.py does the 'master'/'direct'<->1.0/2.0 translation instead. default=0.0 (kRoutingDestFilter's ordinal) is assumed by that same-enum convention, NOT independently confirmed -- genuine absent-key behavior was never isolated since real content only ever writes 1.0/2.0 explicitly. Where FX Bus 1's OWN processed signal (after passing through its FX chain) rejoins the main path -- distinct from GLOBAL_PARAMS['kParamFXBus1Vol'] (that bus's aggregate level) and ROUTING_SLOT_PARAMS['kParamFXBus1Level'] (how much of a given source is SENT into the bus to begin with).

lfo1.mono.notes: Found live 2026-07-29 diagnosing a recreated preset that still sounded '8-bit' after fixing the LFO shape/filter/warp-lane gaps: the real preset's user reported its LFO visibly kept moving even with no note held, while the recreation's didn't -- traced to this key, present (always =1.0 when present, 63/4374 real LFO slots surveyed) only on that preset's busiest LFO (rate 100, RandomSH shape, driving a fast-arpeggiated oscillator). lfo1.rate.notes:
Hz/BPM mapping depends on kParamMode and beat-sync flags. Two points known from 2026-07-29 live UI probing (beat-synced regime): with kParamBeatSync absent (its own true default), setting the RATE knob to exactly '1/8' writes kParamRate=10.66; setting it back to '1/4' makes Serum omit the key again -- i.e. '1/4' BPM-synced IS the genuine absent-state default (not a UI placeholder), confirming mapping.py's omit-when-default fix is correct. 

**RETRACTED AND CORRECTED 2026-08-01**: a 2026-07-31 attempt to calibrate the separate FREE (beat_sync=False) Hz curve produced a bogus, wildly non-monotonic 'result' (a fake exponential-doubling shape at low raw values, anomalous plateaus above raw~35) -- traced to a REAL bug, not a Serum quirk: LfoSpec.beat_sync used to be a plain `bool` defaulting to `False`, which is indistinguishable from 'not set' once mapping.py's omit-at-default logic runs -- so EVERY calibration preset in that sweep silently omitted kParamBeatSync entirely and was actually measured in Serum's real absent-state default (BPM-SYNCED), not free-Hz mode at all. Found live by a user manually turning a calibration preset's RATE knob in Serum and noticing it displayed 'BPM'/a note fraction (e.g. '1/16') instead of Hz -- the automated pipeline never would have caught this on its own, since it only ever inspected the rendered AUDIO, not the loaded preset's own UI state. Fixed by making `LfoSpec.beat_sync` a 3-state `bool | None` (see its docstring) so `False` genuinely writes `kParamBeatSync=False` instead of being omitted.

**Re-calibrated 2026-08-01 with the fix in place, genuine free-Hz mode confirmed this time**: raw 2/5/10/20/30 measured 2.0/5.0/10.0/20.0/30.0 Hz -- an exact 1:1 match, i.e. **raw kParamRate IS literal Hz** in free mode, no curve needed at all (trust this for raw <= ~30). raw=0 (which still omits kParamRate itself, a separate and correct omission -- see _LFO_KEYS_OMIT_AT_DEFAULT) measured 6.25Hz, presumably Serum's own genuine free-mode rate default; not independently confirmed.

**The raw>=~35-40 'anomaly' -- live-Serum cross-check 2026-08-01, resolved as a measurement-pipeline limitation, NOT a real Serum DSP issue.** First live check found real visible/audible glitches -- but traced entirely to the well-known per-voice LFO phase-reset-on-note-on behavior (see LfoSpec.mono's docstring), an artifact of testing with a looping/retriggering piano-roll note, not the rate curve. Re-tested with `mono=True` (removes the retrigger confound) sweeping RATE 20-100%: STILL saw visible 'jumps' at the high end, but explicitly confirmed INAUDIBLE -- consistent with a stroboscopic/ aliasing illusion (the cyclic knob motion beating against the screen's own refresh rate), a known visual-perception effect, not a real audio glitch. **Conclusion**: no evidence of a genuine Serum DSP anomaly at any rate tested -- the real audio is smooth throughout, confirmed by ear with the retrigger confound removed. lfo4.rate.notes:
Hz/BPM mapping depends on kParamMode and beat-sync flags. Two points known from 2026-07-29 live UI probing (beat-synced regime): with kParamBeatSync absent (its own true default), setting the RATE knob to exactly '1/8' writes kParamRate=10.66; setting it back to '1/4' makes Serum omit the key again -- i.e. '1/4' BPM-synced IS the genuine absent-state default (not a UI placeholder), confirming mapping.py's omit-when-default fix is correct. 

**RETRACTED AND CORRECTED 2026-08-01**: a 2026-07-31 attempt to calibrate the separate FREE (beat_sync=False) Hz curve produced a bogus, wildly non-monotonic 'result' (a fake exponential-doubling shape at low raw values, anomalous plateaus above raw~35) -- traced to a REAL bug, not a Serum quirk: LfoSpec.beat_sync used to be a plain `bool` defaulting to `False`, which is indistinguishable from 'not set' once mapping.py's omit-at-default logic runs -- so EVERY calibration preset in that sweep silently omitted kParamBeatSync entirely and was actually measured in Serum's real absent-state default (BPM-SYNCED), not free-Hz mode at all. Found live by a user manually turning a calibration preset's RATE knob in Serum and noticing it displayed 'BPM'/a note fraction (e.g. '1/16') instead of Hz -- the automated pipeline never would have caught this on its own, since it only ever inspected the rendered AUDIO, not the loaded preset's own UI state. Fixed by making `LfoSpec.beat_sync` a 3-state `bool | None` (see its docstring) so `False` genuinely writes `kParamBeatSync=False` instead of being omitted.

**Re-calibrated 2026-08-01 with the fix in place, genuine free-Hz mode confirmed this time**: raw 2/5/10/20/30 measured 2.0/5.0/10.0/20.0/30.0 Hz -- an exact 1:1 match, i.e. **raw kParamRate IS literal Hz** in free mode, no curve needed at all (trust this for raw <= ~30). raw=0 (which still omits kParamRate itself, a separate and correct omission -- see _LFO_KEYS_OMIT_AT_DEFAULT) measured 6.25Hz, presumably Serum's own genuine free-mode rate default; not independently confirmed.

**The raw>=~35-40 'anomaly' -- live-Serum cross-check 2026-08-01, resolved as a measurement-pipeline limitation, NOT a real Serum DSP issue.** First live check found real visible/audible glitches -- but traced entirely to the well-known per-voice LFO phase-reset-on-note-on behavior (see LfoSpec.mono's docstring), an artifact of testing with a looping/retriggering piano-roll note, not the rate curve. Re-tested with `mono=True` (removes the retrigger confound) sweeping RATE 20-100%: STILL saw visible 'jumps' at the high end, but explicitly confirmed INAUDIBLE -- consistent with a stroboscopic/ aliasing illusion (the cyclic knob motion beating against the screen's own refresh rate), a known visual-perception effect, not a real audio glitch. **Conclusion**: no evidence of a genuine Serum DSP anomaly at any rate tested -- the real audio is smooth throughout, confirmed by ear with the retrigger confound removed. The automated pipeline's earlier non-monotonic Hz readings (raw 40/60/80 all reading an identical 21.6Hz, 50/70/90/100 giving inconsistent values) are now understood to be a limitation of `detect_modulation_rate_hz` itself at fast target rates (see its own docstring's 2 documented caveats), not a real curve kink -- don't re-litigate raw>=35 as a Serum bug going forward, but also don't trust the pipeline's own Hz number that fast, only that the underlying audio is well-behaved. See docs/PARAMETER_SCHEMA.md item 6a for the full writeup and reference-serum-verify-audio-pipeline for the pipeline-side notes.

**Re-calibrated 2026-08-01 with the fix in place, genuine free-Hz mode confirmed this time**: raw 2/5/10/20/30 measured 2.0/5.0/10.0/20.0/30.0 Hz -- an exact 1:1 match, i.e. **raw kParamRate IS literal Hz** in free mode, no curve needed at all (trust this for raw <= ~30). raw=0 (which still omits kParamRate itself, a separate and correct omission -- see _LFO_KEYS_OMIT_AT_DEFAULT) measured 6.25Hz, presumably Serum's own genuine free-mode rate default; not independently confirmed.

**The raw>=~35-40 'anomaly' -- live-Serum cross-check 2026-08-01, resolved as a measurement-pipeline limitation, NOT a real Serum DSP issue.** First live check found real visible/audible glitches -- but traced entirely to the well-known per-voice LFO phase-reset-on-note-on behavior (see LfoSpec.mono's docstring), an artifact of testing with a looping/retriggering piano-roll note, not the rate curve. Re-tested with `mono=True` (removes the retrigger confound) sweeping RATE 20-100%: STILL saw visible 'jumps' at the high end, but explicitly confirmed INAUDIBLE -- consistent with a stroboscopic/ aliasing illusion (the cyclic knob motion beating against the screen's own refresh rate), a known visual-perception effect, not a real audio glitch. **Conclusion**: no evidence of a genuine Serum DSP anomaly at any rate tested -- the real audio is smooth throughout, confirmed by ear with the retrigger confound removed. The automated pipeline's earlier non-monotonic Hz readings (raw 40/60/80 all reading an identical 21.6Hz, 50/70/90/100 giving inconsistent values) are now understood to be a limitation of `detect_modulation_rate_hz` itself at fast target rates (see its own docstring's 2 documented caveats), not a real curve kink -- don't re-litigate raw>=35 as a Serum bug going forward, but also don't trust the pipeline's own Hz number that fast, only that the underlying audio is well-behaved. See docs/PARAMETER_SCHEMA.md item 6a for the full writeup and reference-serum-verify-audio-pipeline for the pipeline-side notes.

matrix.mod.ui_name: MOD -- hypothesized separate modulation-mode control (does not exist as a discrete Matrix column)

audit_sources.ref: Official Xfer Serum 2 User Guide (xferrecords.com/manual/serum-2/docs), cited by user 2026-09-16: complete Matrix column specification given as 'SOURCE | CRV | AMOUNT | POL | DESTINATION | OUT | AUX SOURCE | INV | CRV | OUTPUT' -- no MOD column listed.

Serum 2.0.21 MATRIX panel, live UI header zoom, 2026-09-15/16: exact column headers confirmed as SOURCE/CRV/AMOUNT/POL/DESTINATION/OUT/AUX SOURCE/INV/CRV/OUTPUT -- matches official spec exactly, no MOD column present.

5 independent negative UI checks 2026-09-15/16: AMOUNT right-click context menu (only 'Mod{N} Amount'/Reset Control/MIDI Learn/Lock Parameter), SOURCE right-click (only source-selector menu), drag-handle right-click (no menu), MATRIX-level MENU dropdown (Sort by Source/Sort by Destination/Lock Matrix/Create Vibrato/Create Velo->Amp/Apply and Delete Macros -- no MOD item), Serum global hamburger MENU (About/Presets/MIDI Map/MPE settings -- no MOD item).

matrix.mod.notes: PROMOTED 2026-09-16 from UNVERIFIED_CANDIDATE per official Xfer Serum 2 User Guide, which gives the complete, authoritative Matrix column specification and contains no MOD column -- this matches the live UI's exact column set with zero discrepancy. Combined with 5 independent negative UI checks (context menus, both Matrix-level and Serum global menus), this meets the project's evidence bar for a considered negative finding (official comprehensive-source + multiple independent live-UI checks). The modulation-mode behavior originally hypothesized under 'MOD' is fully and exactly distributed across existing controls: AMOUNT (bidirectional -- negative depth inverts the source before reaching destination), POL (bipolar/unipolar), AUX SOURCE (secondary amount-scaling source), INV (inverts aux source), CRV x2 (primary and aux curve shaping), and OUTPUT (final output scale). No separate MOD identity is created.

matrix.routing.signal_balance.notes: Recorded as ONE consolidated structural record rather than 19 individual semantic_ids, since all 19 share a single semantic identity (modulating what fraction of a given signal source's output flows to the main Filter chain vs BUS1 vs BUS2), parametrized by (source, target) rather than being 19 independently-meaningful control types. audit_sources.ref: Serum 2.0.21 MATRIX panel, live UI, 2026-09-16, THREE test attempts: Attempt 1 & 2 (negative/no-op): rows with a Macro as DESTINATION only (e.g. '-'->Macro2, '-'->Macro3, both Macros at default/untouched 0 value) -> invoked Apply and Delete Macros -> AFTER=no visible change to either row, confirming operation does not act on Macro-as-destination rows regardless of the destination macro's own value. Attempt 3 (positive/root-caused): used MATRIX.SYS.EXPANDED_VIEW to access physical Macro knobs; set a fresh row SOURCE=Macro1 (dragged Macro1 knob to non-zero, confirmed via zoom), DESTINATION=Macro2 (Macro2 knob still untouched at 0) -- note Serum's SOURCE dropdown greys out 'Macro 2' as selectable when Macro 2 is already that same row's own DESTINATION (prevents same-row self-reference) -> Matrix menu->Apply and Delete Macros -> AFTER: (a) the Macro1->Macro2 row COMPLETELY DELETED, reverted to empty '-'/'-'; (b) Macro 2's own knob value CHANGED from 0 to non-zero (confirmed via zoom, new blue arc appeared) -- the modulation amount was baked in as a static offset to Macro 2's base value; (c) Macro 1's knob value UNCHANGED (the source macro itself is untouched, only the routing FROM it is removed).

matrix.sys.apply_and_delete_macros.notes: NEW 2026-09-16, root-caused after 2 false-negative attempts. CONFIRMED SEMANTIC: operation finds all Matrix rows where a Macro is acting as SOURCE, bakes the live modulation effect into the destination's base/static value, then deletes those specific rows -- committing macro-driven modulation as a permanent value and severing the macro's live control over that destination. Distinct from the per-macro right-click 'apply and delete A macro' singular operation (MACRO.SYS.APPLY_AND_DELETE_MACRO) found during MACRO section closure -- this resolves that record's previously-flagged 'residual open question for the MATRIX sweep' cross-reference.

matrix.sys.create_vibrato.ui_name: Create Vibrato (Unused LFO->Pitch via Wheel) -- quick-setup macro operation

audit_sources.ref: Official Xfer Serum 2 User Guide (xferrecords.com/manual/serum-2/docs), cited by user 2026-09-16: 'Create a new modulation mapping the next available LFO to Main Tuning using the Mod Wheel.'

Serum 2.0.21 MATRIX panel, live UI, 2026-09-16, TWO independent invocations from a controlled baseline: (1) BEFORE=LFO1 present as SOURCE in one row with DESTINATION=Off (inactive/unused), LFO2 present as SOURCE elsewhere with DESTINATION=Macro3 (active/used) -> Matrix menu->Create Vibrato -> AFTER=NEW row created: SOURCE=LFO1, DESTINATION=Main Tuning, AUX SOURCE=Mod Wheel, AMOUNT/POL defaulted -- confirms 'unused' means 'SOURCE present but its own DESTINATION=Off', not 'absent from all rows'. (2) 2nd invocation immediately after -> AFTER=ANOTHER new row: SOURCE=LFO3 (correctly skipped LFO1 and LFO2, now both 'used'), DESTINATION=Main Tuning, AUX SOURCE=Mod Wheel -- proves operation is NOT idempotent/toggle (creates a new row every invocation) and proves the exact LFO-selection rule (next LFO in numeric order whose current DESTINATION is Off).

(A) Mod Wheel->Macro 1 duplicated exactly in a second row: ACCEPTED as independent route, Macro 1 modulator-count badge read 2, clearing one duplicate left the other fully intact. (B) Mod Wheel->Macro 2 added alongside Mod Wheel->Macro 1: ACCEPTED, no conflict. matrix.sys.duplicate_route_policy.notes: NEW RECORD 2026-09-15 (Phase 2C Test 2, formalized). The MATRIX imposes no uniqueness constraint on (SOURCE, DESTINATION) route pairs. Every route is an independent, separately-addressable object: duplicate SOURCE/DESTINATION pairs coexist without merging, replacing, or rejecting; clearing one route via SOURCE=Off never affects any other route, including an exact duplicate of itself. Destinations with multiple simultaneous modulators sum/stack (confirmed via Serum's own per-destination modulator-count badge incrementing correctly with each additional route).

Checked Options menu: 'Audio Engine On' is already checked in Ableton, indicating the block is Serum-instance-specific, not an Ableton-wide transport/engine issue -- likely an audio-driver/device configuration matter outside safe UI-only exploration scope.

Serum 2.0.21 / Ableton Live 12.3, live UI, 2026-09-16, THIRD resolution attempt: (1) Options>Settings>Audio panel inspected -- Driver Type=ASIO, Audio Device=Steinberg built-in ASIO Driver, Sample Rate=44100, Buffer=441 samples, Overall Latency=1.09ms -- all properly configured, rules out a no-device-selected issue. (2) Clicked track-header collapse toggle (top-left icon next to device chain title) which revealed the actual Ableton track header sidebar (previously hidden behind the maximized Serum device panel): showed MIDI From=All Ins, MIDI Channel=All Channels, Monitor=Auto, Audio To=Main, and a volume fader displaying -inf dB. Attempted to raise the volume fader via drag and via scroll-wheel at its coordinates -- neither produced a visible value change, indicating either the fader is not interactive at this compressed sidebar width or the coordinates missed the actual control target. Re-collapsed the sidebar cleanly with no adverse state change.

Serum 2.0.21 / Ableton Live 12.3, live UI, 2026-09-16, FOURTH and most exhaustive resolution attempt per explicit user task list: (1) Disabled Options>View>Plug-In Windows to force Serum out of maximized floating-window mode and reveal Ableton full Arrangement view (transport bar, timeline, track headers) -- this was the key missing step in prior attempts, which had been testing only within a maximized/floating Serum panel. (2) Confirmed via full transport bar: clicked Ableton native Play button -- playhead position counter demonstrably advanced across multiple screenshots (bar 1211->1220->1230->1235->1247->1254), CONFIRMING genuine active playback, not merely a UI state change. (3) Re-examined track 1 mixer strip at full Arrangement-view size: volume shows a teal readout of 0 (likely 0dB/unity, not -inf as initially misread from the compressed sidebar in the prior session -- the -inf values visible are the live PEAK METERS showing no current signal, a separate and expected reading when idle). (4) Stopped transport, navigated back into Serum device view via device-chain expand triangle. (5) Directly clicked Serum on-screen piano keyboard (multiple positions tested) to trigger a note independent of any Arrangement clip content. RESULT: Audio processing disabled warning banner persisted through ALL of the above -- engine-on, device-configured, transport-actively-running, and direct-note-click conditions were all satisfied simultaneously at various points, yet the warning never cleared.
